purpose: Resolve the highest-information fog identified by the M-04B adversarial self-trial: post-Cold War externalization, deliberate market shaping, institutional replacement, dependency, and the incomplete population-data-to-consequence chain. The wave separates bounded lane support from the unproved system-wide coordinated-capture proposition.

method.null_hypothesis: ordinary shared ecology and structural convergence
method.promotion_rule: A bounded proposition may be marked supported_for_human_review only when an operative public record establishes the required transition. No local result promotes a broader network, organism, coercion, extraction, or wrongdoing claim.
method.mirror_rule: Where an official SAM.gov notice exposes an attachment but the attachment bytes are not yet in repository custody, a public text mirror may support triage only. Primary attachment bytes remain a named acquisition requirement.

records.proposition: Post-Cold War defense retrenchment reduced public acquisition capacity while contractor reliance and contracted-service management risk increased.

sources.title: High-Risk Series: Dedicated Leadership Needed to Address Limited Progress in Most High-Risk Areas

records.observation: GAO states that DOD reduced its acquisition workforce in the mid-1990s as defense budgets fell, later rebuilt that workforce amid skill-gap concerns and growing contractor reliance, and continued to face long-standing service-acquisition and operational-contractor-support problems.
supports: P1 lean-hegemon externalization as a documented historical substrate
a dated capacity-loss and contractor-reliance transition
continuity from workforce reduction into later contract-management risk
does_not_support: continuity into any named present-day platform without additional records
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the 1990s force-structure, acquisition-workforce, service-contract, systems-integration, and outsourcing instruments needed to connect specific transferred public capabilities to P2 and P3 institutions.
records.falsifier: Contemporaneous records show no material public-capacity reduction, no substitution by contracted capacity, or no persistence into later service-acquisition dependence.

records.proposition: Palantir deliberately used a formal legal challenge to change the Army's DCGS-A2 acquisition gate toward statutorily required consideration of commercial alternatives.

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc. v. United States, Appeal No. 17-1465

records.observation: The Federal Circuit affirmed that the Army had failed to satisfy 10 U.S.C. section 2377 before proceeding with DCGS-A2 and required compliance before award, while expressly declining to require selection of Palantir. A later award notice records Palantir as the Capability Drop 1 awardee.
supports: I2 deliberate market shaping in one bounded procurement lane
a documented actor action, gate challenge, judicial result, and changed acquisition constraint
effective judicial counterpower against an inadequately supported acquisition approach
does_not_support: a direct causal claim that the appellate judgment alone produced the later award
common design with investors, banks, policy groups, or other vendors
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the complete post-injunction solicitation, evaluation, source-selection, technical-baseline, data-rights, acceptance, performance, protest, and unsuccessful-offeror record.
records.falsifier: The post-injunction record shows no material gate change, no commercial-item consideration, or a later award process wholly independent of the challenged requirement structure.

records.proposition: The Army converted many Palantir procurements into a ten-year enterprise purchasing framework.

sources.title: U.S. Army Awards Enterprise Service Agreement to Enhance Military Readiness and Drive Operational Efficiency
Palantir Enterprise Agreement award and J&A notice

records.observation: The Army states that the agreement consolidates 75 contracts, including 15 prime and 60 related contracts, into one vehicle for up to ten years with a maximum potential value of $10 billion; the ceiling is not an obligation or commitment.
supports: C3 public conversion into an enterprise acquisition vehicle
cross-program consolidation and a durable purchasing framework
a bounded option-set and public-gate transition
does_not_support: $10 billion in actual obligations or outlays
institutional replacement without the underlying J&A and operating evidence
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Preserve the official J&A bytes and enumerate every consolidated contract, order, obligation, user community, mission, performance measure, competitor, termination term, and transition right.
records.falsifier: The vehicle remains administratively convenient but nonexclusive, lightly used, readily substitutable, and without material operating consolidation.

records.proposition: Palantir had become a practical operating layer in bounded Army enterprise and warfighting domains, with transition costs the Army considered operationally unacceptable.

sources.title: A02 TAB B - Palantir EA Final J&A 03JUL2025 v2 Redacted
Public text rendering of the Army Palantir EA J&A

records.observation: The J&A text describes a proprietary, highly customized and integrated Palantir environment; growing Army dependence across enterprise and warfighting domains; complete rebuilding, complex migration, reaccreditation, workflow disruption, and institutional-knowledge loss if another vendor replaced it; and sole-source necessity for continuity. It also states that the Government retains unlimited rights and ownership in Government data and transformations while Palantir retains its commercial software.
supports: I3 institutional replacement in a bounded Army lane
C5 technical and operational dependency
documented switching costs and continuity constraints
a mixed control-rights result: government data rights alongside proprietary platform rights
does_not_support: the absence of any feasible phased exit
coordination with a broader founder-controlled network
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire official J&A bytes, Attachment 01, all 15 prime contract files, interface-control and ontology documentation, data-export tests, independent transition estimates, actual replacement exercises, performance records, and order-level competition evidence.
records.falsifier: Operational testing shows the Government can export data and workflows, reaccredit an alternative, preserve mission continuity, and replace the platform at proportionate cost and schedule.

records.proposition: Palantir's ICM platform functions as ICE's integrated investigative case-management and analytics operating layer, with documented proprietary and transition dependencies.

sources.title: ICE J&A-25-0266 Investigative Case Management limited-sources notice
Public text rendering of ICE J&A-25-0266

records.observation: The limited-sources justification describes ICM as ICE's official investigative-case system of record and operational backbone, joining subject records and external law-enforcement data in one case-management and analytics platform. ICE assessed 42 vendors, described alternatives as requiring extensive redevelopment and 18-to-24-month transitions, stated that switching would disrupt investigations, and identified Palantir as sole owner of the platform software and source code. The same record requires ICE ownership of transactional and derived analytical data and return of Government information.
supports: I3 institutional replacement in a bounded ICE investigative lane
C5 practical dependency, switching cost, accreditation and continuity constraints
a partial H3 chain from subject data and joins through investigative analytics and case workflow
explicit public-versus-private rights allocation
does_not_support: a specific detention, removal, denial, arrest, or other consequence caused by ICM
the accuracy or fairness of a classification
private ownership of ICE transactional or derived analytical data
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Preserve official LSJ bytes; obtain the data dictionary, ontology, source-system inventory, workflow and approval rules, role permissions, audit logs, error/correction records, consequence-specific case traces, transition plan, and observed data-export tests.
records.falsifier: The operative record shows ICM is replaceable without material mission disruption, does not occupy the described case-and-analytics role, or is not used in any consequential investigative workflow.

records.proposition: Independent oversight has identified data-quality and reporting controls that ICE must implement inside ICM.

sources.publisher: DHS Office of Inspector General via Oversight.gov
sources.title: ICE Did Not Accurately Measure and Report Its Progress in Disrupting or Dismantling Transnational Criminal Organizations

records.observation: DHS OIG found that ICE HSI did not accurately measure and report TCO disruption and recommended that special agents identify in ICM whether each Significant Case Report involves an entity meeting HSI's TCO definition.
supports: ICM's role in consequential investigative reporting workflows
an identified control weakness and an independent counterpower intervention
the need to distinguish system capability from complete or accurate operational use
does_not_support: that ICM generated the inaccurate classification
that the recommendation was fully implemented
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the full report, management response, implementation evidence, ICM field definition, completion rates, validation rules, audit logs, and later measurement outcomes.
records.falsifier: The relevant reporting field and workflow are outside ICM, the recommendation was based on a mistaken system attribution, or subsequent evidence shows no material control weakness.

records.proposition: The current estate can connect Palantir ICM to ICE's detention/release risk-classification consequences.

sources.publisher: DHS Office of Inspector General via Oversight.gov
sources.title: ICE's Risk Classification Assessment Process Was Not Consistently Used to Prevent the Release of High-Risk Individuals

records.observation: DHS OIG reports that ICE officers were responsible for detention/release risk assessments for most detained noncitizens and that assessments were not conducted for 79,977 people in FY2023 and 129,250 in FY2022. The source does not identify ICM or Palantir as the risk-assessment system.
supports: a bounded affected population, consequential decision class, human responsibility, and control failure
the existence of a real H3/H4 consequence-and-oversight lane
does_not_support: the missing join from ICM data or analytics to the detention/release assessment
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the risk-classification system name, contract, data sources, decision rules, user interface, audit trail, relation to ICM or EID/ERO systems, override and appeal records, and case-level chronology before making any platform-to-consequence claim.
records.falsifier: The risk-classification process is technically and operationally independent of ICM and receives no material ICM-derived data or workflow input.

records.proposition: The bounded Palantir, Army, ICE, investor, banking, and policy records establish one deliberately coordinated founder-controlled capture system.
records.observation: The newly resolved records establish historical externalization, one deliberate procurement-gate intervention, and two bounded institutional-replacement/dependency lanes. They do not supply cross-entity governance, shared planning, two-sided transactions, common operating design, or a complete population-consequence-to-private-benefit chain.
supports: continued investigation of repeated public-conversion and platform-dependency mechanisms
does_not_support: common design across companies, funds, banks, policy institutions, and public agencies
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require exact cross-entity governance or planning records, transaction-specific rights, interoperable operating records, common doctrine connected to decisions, two-sided theater transfers, consequence chains, and public-risk/private-benefit chronology.
records.falsifier: Complete denominators and operative records show independent procurement, ordinary specialization, practical alternatives, effective counterpower, and no cross-entity common design.
